title.purpose: App names, revision roles, panel heads.

label.purpose: Captions, readouts, units note, contact field names, colophon, scroll hint.

data.purpose: Title-block fields, table heads, tags, zone markers.

dimension.purpose: Dimension values, dates, balloon and note numerals, measured values.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for every state transition (0.2s) and entrance (0.9-1.6s).

motion.name: hero-explode
motion.value: scroll-scrubbed translateZ, layer gap g0 to g1 over first 70% of a 240vh track; rotateX 56 to 61deg, rotateZ -42 to -34deg; 1.6s intro ease-apart on load
motion.purpose: Signature: the hero assembly explodes into five layers; callouts re-projected to 2D every frame.

motion.name: isometric-to-elevation
motion.value: scroll-scrubbed rotateX 58 to 0deg, rotateZ +/-40 to 0deg, y 80 to 0px, perspective 1400px; callouts and dimension fade in over the last 18%
motion.purpose: App drawings settle from isometric into a front elevation before annotation.

motion.name: sheet-exit-tilt
motion.value: scroll-scrubbed rotateX 0 to 16deg, scale 1 to 0.88, opacity 1 to 0.2, perspective 1600px, origin bottom centre
motion.purpose: Each sheet leans back and recedes as it leaves.

motion.name: revision-swing
motion.value: rotateX -70 to 0deg, 0.9s on ease, once in view
motion.purpose: Revision rows swing down into place.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: MotionConfig reducedMotion=user; every scroll transform resolves to its final value; smooth scroll off
motion.purpose: Everything static and readable under prefers-reduced-motion.

narrative.overview:
Every page is a sheet in an engineering drawing set: a graphite sheet laid on a darker desk, framed twice, lettered along its edges with zone numbers (1 to 8) and zone letters (A to F), and closed by a title block that states the drawing name, sheet number of the set, revision, scale and projection. Content is not placed in cards; it is drawn. Work is shown as assemblies with balloons and leader lines, experience as a revision table, skills as a bill of materials, contact as an approval block.

The linework is flat and precise. Vellum-grey lines in three weights do all the structural work, white is reserved for lettering that must be read first, and safety orange marks only what a drafter would mark in red: leaders, dimensions, balloons, the current revision, and the primary action. Depth exists only as real projection (isometric views, explodes, sheets tilting away), never as decoration.

Motion is the drawing being operated: the hero assembly explodes along its stack as the visitor scrolls, app drawings rotate from isometric into a front elevation and only then gain their callouts, and each sheet leans back and recedes as it leaves, like turning to the next sheet. All of it is scroll-scrubbed with an exponential ease-out, and all of it resolves to a static, fully readable drawing under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite sheet on a darker desk, with a 32px drafting grid at near-invisible strength.
Double frame, zone markers and a per-sheet title block on every section.
Square corners everywhere; circles only for balloons, leader terminators and sheet numbers.
Expanded uppercase Archivo for all lettering; B612 Mono only for numbers, dates and table field data.
One accent, safety orange, carrying drafting meaning rather than decoration.
Scroll-scrubbed 3D projection that collapses to a static drawing under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Red Pencil Rule
rules.body: Safety orange marks drafting meaning (a leader, a dimension, a balloon, a revision, the current state) or the one primary action. If an orange element could be removed without losing a measurement, a reference or the CV/email action, it should not be orange.

rules.name: The White Lettering Rule
rules.body: Pure white is for lettering a visitor must read first (names, headings, callout titles, values) and for the drawn device outline. Running text stays in Vellum Line.

rules.name: The Mono Means Measured Rule
rules.body: B612 Mono appears only on numbers, dates, units and table or field metadata. Prose, headings, buttons and callout titles are always Archivo.

rules.name: The One Annotation Hand Rule
rules.body: Every caption-level note uses the `--annot` lettering token. A new note style is a new token, not a local font declaration.

rules.name: The Projection, Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: If something needs to read as in front, move it in z or draw it with a heavier or brighter line. Do not add a shadow, glow or blur.

dos: **Do** give every new section a sheet: frame, zone markers, and a title block with its own drawing name and sheet number.
**Do** letter in expanded uppercase Archivo (width 110-125%) and keep numbers, dates and field names in B612 Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** use the `--annot` token for every caption, readout and field note.
**Do** connect any annotation to its subject with an orange leader and balloon, and knock text out on Graphite Sheet where lines pass behind it.
**Do** express layers and materials with hatching and dashed outlines.
**Do** drive motion from scroll with the exponential ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), and make every motion value resolve to its final, readable state when reduced motion is requested.
donts: **Don't** use orange for decoration, large backgrounds or secondary actions; the approval block and primary button are the only orange fills.
**Don't** add drop shadows, glows, glass blur or smooth colour gradients; linear gradients are allowed only to draw grid lines and hatching.
**Don't** round UI corners; reserve curves for balloons, terminators and drawn devices.
**Don't** set prose, headings or buttons in mono.
**Don't** put white on running text or let the faint line carry text.
**Don't** use content cards or a bento grid; place content as drawings, tables and notes on the sheet.
